headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: MemMachine’s MCP/API outputs can be fed into LightZero only via external orchestration, while direct data leakage and write conflicts are limited by LightZero’s no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no shared channel or parser surface, so direct injection is not shown. But MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, and LightZero can be orchestrated externally; if MemMachine output is copied into LightZero prompts or files, instruction-like content could be misread. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF an operator copies MemMachine-generated text into LightZero prompts or files
IF a wrapper agent forwards MemMachine MCP output to LightZero without sanitization
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from MemMachine output
Add a manual review step before any copy-paste into LightZero
Prefix imported text as untrusted data
requires-engineering: build provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero cannot read files or use network egress, so it is not a strong leakage source. MemMachine does touch long-term user facts and conversational context, but the pair lacks a shared workspace or authenticated data path in the profiles. Leakage is therefore limited to unusual external bridging, not a default pairwise flow.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same external workspace or clipboard
IF MemMachine context is manually exported into LightZero inputs
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable clipboard sharing during handoff
Redact personal facts before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem write, subprocess, or network egress, so it cannot materially conflict on shared mutable resources. MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API access, but no overlapping write scope is documented. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator granting both write access, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF MemMachine is configured to mutate shared state through its API while LightZero is wrapped with write privileges
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only
Avoid shared mutable directories
Serialize any shared updates through one controller
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is an agentic travel-planning system with MCP/API access, so it can plausibly act on upstream text. LightZero is a game-playing system and does not verify downstream facts. If MemMachine consumes LightZero-generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect plans or actions. The interaction is inferred, but the risk is real enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine treats LightZero output as factual input without verification
IF LightZero-generated text is routed into MemMachine planning or action steps
mitigations: Require source attribution on all transferred outputs
Add a verification checklist before MemMachine acts
Limit LightZero output to non-factual game-state summaries
requires-engineering: insert a validation layer between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented. LightZero is game-playing and touches no data classes, while MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context. The only compliance concern visible is that MemMachine may retain personal context longer than expected, but the pair does not show a cross-border or regulated-data transfer path.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into MemMachine
IF that data is exported into a separate system with stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid entering regulated data into MemMachine
Set a short retention policy in the host system
Document what data classes are allowed
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows
